fixes.explanation: Amos says, “She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.” Picture reaching for a hand and finding empty air. That's the whole scene, and it's a heavy one. The passage calls it a lamentation, and I think that's why it sounds so sorrowful.
Nine hundred sounds like a city that came through okay, and I wish it did. But the words are “…will have but a hundred left…” It's a hundred that remain, not nine hundred.

The LORD says, “…the one that marches out a hundred strong will have but ten left in the house of Israel.” Smaller city, smaller number, same shape. Both lose nine out of every ten. You spotted the pattern.

The LORD says, “…Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.” Those are the places He just warned them not to seek or go to. Seeking them leads nowhere. He wants them to seek Him instead.

The LORD says, “…He will sweep like fire through the house of Joseph…” That's a serious warning, and it says the fire “…will devour everything…” Seeking Him is the way to live. I think that's why the call to seek Him comes right before it.
False it is. The fire “…will devour everything, with no one at Bethel to extinguish it.” So there's no one at Bethel to put it out. The only safe move is to seek the LORD.
Boundary stones are a fair thing to think of, but they don't show up in this verse. The LORD says, “You oppress the righteous by taking bribes…” Bribes are the answer here. Stay with what's written.

Edom, a nation, doesn't appear in this verse. It says, “Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.” A remnant is what's left. The remnant of Joseph is who the perhaps is for.
The verse says, “The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.” Even the farmer gets called in. The grief reaches wide. You got it.

A farmer feels like someone busy enough to be left out, but the text includes him. “The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.” So true is the answer. The farmer is named right there in the verse.
